newsitem.title: GERMANY: German direct marketing association sees boom.
newsitem.headline: German direct marketing association sees boom.

text.p: The German direct marketing association (DDV) said on Friday its industry was in the midst of a boom and expected a 10 percent boost in turnover for 1997.
The DDV said direct marketing posted 30 billion marks in sales for 1996 and predicted a jump to 33 billion marks for the current year.
"In Germany, almost every second mark spent on advertising goes to direct marketing," DDV president Friedhelm Lammoth said. "The days when traditional advertising could stand alone are over."
The largest share of direct-marketing income, the DDV said, goes toward direct mailing. Last year, direct mail accounted for 9.2 billion marks of direct-marketing turnover.
The DDV comprises 740 members, including telephone marketing companies, mailing list distributors and media companies which carry direct-marketing advertising.
